headline: Your PC's 'Secure Boot' Feature Has Been Broken for a Decade
reasoning: This topic scores highly due to its immense clickability and mainstream appeal; the core idea that a fundamental security feature on most PCs has been broken for a decade is shocking and easy to grasp. While its direct practical value is low for the average user, it excels as a 'hot take' or 'explainer' piece, fitting our 'industry drama' vertical and appealing to anyone who wants to stay informed about the technology they use daily.
summary: A core security feature in Windows and Linux, Secure Boot, was discovered to be easily bypassable for over a decade due to Microsoft's failure to revoke old, vulnerable code. This flaw could allow attackers with physical access to install malicious firmware that survives an OS reinstall.

source_articles.title: Microsoft’s Secure Boot has been broken for a decade and no one noticed until now
source_articles.excerpt: Old and forgotten "shims" Microsoft failed to revoke have made Secure Boot bypasses simple.
